description:
MEASURED s460ao (agent AO, round 17).  The task's own instruction was "measure
before building"; the measurement CONFIRMS the diagnosis and BOUNDS the prize
at far less than ARM A's, so nothing was built.  A bench row `feread2` is now
in tools/bench-exec.pl carrying the shape (element count and outer repeats
matched to `feread` so the two subtract cleanly).

THE DIAGNOSIS IS CORRECT, and here is the proof, not an argument:

    row       raw-elems ON    raw-elems OFF (PCL_RAW_ELEMS=0)
    feread      0.1939 s          0.2798 s      <- raw elements buy 31 %
    feread2     0.5856 s          0.5624 s      <- IDENTICAL, i.e. already
                                                   in the all-boxed world

`feread` gains 31 % from raw elements (the ARM A number, reproduced).
`feread2` gains NOTHING, because `p-flatten-args` has already promoted every
slot of @a and @b — exactly what this task says.  That is the cleanest
possible confirmation and it took two bench runs.

BUT THE PRIZE IS NOT ARM A's 40 %.  feread2 is 0.586 s where feread is
0.194 s for the SAME 30M element reads, so ~0.39 s of the row is the
flattener's own per-element work, which no-promote does not touch.  Removing
the promotion recovers only the raw-vs-boxed READ difference — the 31 % of
the read portion, i.e. **~15 % of the row**: 1.25x perl -> ~1.06x, never
feread's 0.46x.  Against that: the fix is an EMISSION change (a no-promote
argument on p-flatten-args, set from the `foreach_ro` verdict), so it costs
the full boat (generation bump, three artifacts, corpus-diff, full sweep,
gate-SET scan) for 2 of the 32 arm sites in the corpus.  RECOMMENDATION: do
not ship it alone; fold it in if the flattener's per-element cost is ever
attacked, since they share the same code.

A PLAUSIBLE CHEAP WIN, MEASURED AND REJECTED — do not retry it.  The
flattener allocates its result `(make-array (length args) ...)`: that is the
count of ARGUMENTS where a count of ELEMENTS is meant, so `f(@a)` with 1000
elements grows from 2 by doubling, copying ~1022 elements per call on top of
the 1000 pushes.  Pre-sizing it from the element count is runtime-only, needs
no emission change, and looks free.  IT IS NOT: the O(1) pre-pass taxes the
overwhelmingly common SCALAR-argument call to save growth in the rare array
one.  A/B, best-of-5, one session:

    fib(27)x  0.4505 -> 0.4676 s  (+3.8 % SLOWER)
    gcdrec    0.1064 -> 0.1088 s  (+2.3 % SLOWER)
    feread2   0.5815 -> 0.5694 s  (-2.1 % faster)

Net negative.  Reverted; the rejection and its numbers are recorded in a
comment above `p-flatten-args` so the next reader does not re-derive it.
This is the s458ak rule firing again: a guard added in front of an existing
fast path must be measured against the path it precedes, not only against the
work it avoids.

ALSO KILLED (a hypothesis that did NOT survive): "the cost is growth-copying,
so array SIZE should change cost per element."  Two shapes with the same 30M
total elements — arrays of 10 x 1.5M flattens vs arrays of 500 x 30k — cost
about the same per element (0.85 s vs 0.72 s wall).  That test does NOT
discriminate, because BOTH grow from `(length args)` = 2; the pre-size A/B
above is what actually settled it.  Recorded so the non-discriminating
experiment is not repeated.

STILL OPEN: the flattener's ~17-20 ns per element (cond dispatch +
vector-push-extend per element) is where feread2's time actually is.  That is
the target worth sizing, and it is runtime-only.


=== DONE (s473r, 2026-09-07) â RE-MEASURED, and the arm lost its row ===

The brief asked for a re-measurement on the merged tree before any work,
because #1182 (`%p-array-grow-discarding`, s473p) changed the growth path.
The re-measurement found something the task could not have known:

**`feread2` NO LONGER REACHES THE FLATTENER AT ALL.**  `for my $x (@a, @b)`
now lowers to

    (p-foreach-raw ($x (vector @a @b)) :arrays t :my t â¦)

â the `foreach-arrays` run (#1184, widened to one array by #1409 in round
30).  `grep -c p-flatten-args` over the emitted feread2 program is **0**.  So
the row this task was sized against (0.586 s, of which "~0.39 s is the
flattener`s own per-element work") measures something else entirely today,
and the round-27 verdict`s feread2 0.28x is the flattener-free number.  ARM A
and this arm were BOTH about that row; both are now moot for it.

WHERE THE FLATTENER STILL IS, measured on the shape that still reaches it â a
sub call with a whole array argument, which has NO standing bench row:

    my @a = (1..1000); sub f { return scalar(@_) }
    for (1..20000) { $s += f(@a) }          # 20 M elements flattened

    perl  0.02 s   (perl ALIASES @a into @_ and copies nothing: O(1) per call)
    PCL   0.35 s, minus the 0.18 s the same program with `f(1)` costs
          = 0.17 s for 20 M elements = **8.5 ns per element**

That is about HALF the 17-20 ns this task recorded, on a shape where perl
does no per-element work at all.  The residue is the `cond` (null / p-box-p /
%p-elem-cell) plus one `vector-push-extend` per element; the promotion itself
is amortised away after an array`s first flatten, exactly as p-flatten-args`
docstring says.

NOT TAKEN, and why: the arm`s own bench row is gone, so a change here could
not be sized against anything standing; the obvious cheap shape (pre-size the
result from the element count) is the arm this task already measured and
KILLED ("do not retry it": fib(27)x +3.8 %, gcdrec +2.3 %); and a bulk
`replace` needs "every element is already a box", which costs a scan of the
same elements unless the array carries that as a FACT.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: a bench row for `f(@a)` (the shape above) plus the
per-array "all elements boxed" flag that would let the copy be a `replace`.
Filed as part of #1517 with these numbers.
subject: #862 ARM A does not pay for a MULTI-array foreach list -- MEASURED s460ao: diagnosis confirmed (feread2 identical with raw-elems on/off), prize bounded at ~15% not ARM A's 40%; pre-sizing the flattener measured NEGATIVE and rejected
